Introduction  
 
 
The Ministry of Public Service and Labour (MIFOTRA) jointly with Rwanda Governance Board 
(RGB), Rwanda Standard Board (RSB), Ministry of Local Government (MINALOC) and 
National Public Service Commission (NPSC) have established the Quality Service Delivery 
Standards that serve as a national service excellence framework to provide orientation on the 
required minimum measurable service quality standards towards customer satisfaction. In order 
attain consistency in quality of service provision, one of the requirements is to have documented 
standard operating procedures (SOPs) for all processes of the public institutions while 
customizing the Quality Service Delivery Standards. 
 
This guide provides guidance on the rationale for documenting institutional SOPs. How they 
should be documented, the minimum contents of SOPs and their approval process.  
 
2 
Rationale for development of Standard Operating Procedures 
 
Institutionalizing the process for documenting procedures to implement policies, laws and 
regulations as well as their daily management and administrative practices increases efficiency in 
public service management by addressing a number of issues:  
 
2.1 
Cost Effectiveness 
 
Availability of a well written SOPs results in the following benefits:  
1 º Less time spent seeking guidance;  
2 º Errors prevention; and  
3 º Consistent and reliable services. 
  
2.2 
Facilitated Induction and Change Management  
 
Well developed and accessible SOPs provide institutional staff with the tools needed to 
effectively move to action and learn quickly how they have to proceed to perform their tasks. 
The SOPs help in streamlining processes and providing a basis for individual and departmental 
accountability.
